Implementation Plan

I have enough to write the plan; no extra evidence is needed. The Phase 1 step and the alt-model wait step match what the issue describes. The workflow is 391,979 bytes, about 38 KB under the 430,000 cap. The clarify failure comment comes from `clarify.yml` (line 2349) using the `GH_PAT` user, so its author is not `github-actions[bot]`. That is why the current check misses it.

## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. Step "Phase 1: Wait for clarify to complete" (`id: wait-clarify`, around line 899)
- **env:** add `CLARIFY_CREATED_AFTER: ${{ steps.create-issue.outputs.created_after }}`. The name is not used anywhere in the file. A script cannot read `${{ }}` at runtime, so the timeout lookup needs this env value. Leave the existing inline expression in `capture_run_id` alone.
- **Extend the existing failure query; do not add a call.** Today the loop reads `LAST_BOT_COMMENT=$(gh_api_safe_print ".../comments?per_page=5&direction=desc" --jq '<bot select>' || echo "")`. Change it to:
  - Make that same single call without `--jq` and store the raw JSON in a new variable, e.g. `CLARIFY_POLL_COMMENTS_JSON=$(gh_api_safe_print "repos/${TEST_REPO}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}/comments?per_page=5&direction=desc" || echo "[]")`. Keep the URL exactly as it is.
  - Work out `LAST_BOT_COMMENT` locally with the old jq expression: `printf '%s' "$CLARIFY_POLL_COMMENTS_JSON" | jq -r '<old expr>' 2>/dev/null || echo ""`. The existing `clarification_needed` branch stays byte-for-byte the same.
  - Work out a new count locally, e.g. `CLARIFY_FAILED_COMMENTS`: `[.[] | select((.author_association // "") | IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR")) | select((.body // "") | startswith("AI clarification workflow failed"))] | length`, with `2>/dev/null || echo 0`. This is the same `IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR")` pattern the orchestrate dispatch step already uses.
  - If the count is a number (`[[ "$CLARIFY_FAILED_COMMENTS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]`) and greater than 0:
    - print `::error::Clarify phase failed — ${CLARIFY_ISSUE_URL} has an 'AI clarification workflow failed' comment`;
    - write `echo "status=clarify_failed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`;
    - `exit 1`.
  - Never echo a comment body.
  - Put this block after the capacity check and before `# Inactivity timeout`. The existing order (`grep -qE 'ai:planning|ai:awaiting-approval'`, then the capacity match, then the capacity status, then "Clarify phase stalled") stays as it is.
- **Issue URL:** define it once before the loop: `CLARIFY_ISSUE_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/${TEST_REPO}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}"`.
- **Timeout branch:** keep the existing `::error::Clarify phase stalled …` line and `status=timeout`. Before `exit 1`, add:
  - `echo "  Issue: ${CLARIFY_ISSUE_URL}"`;
  - if `CLARIFY_CREATED_AFTER` is not empty, look up one run with `CLARIFY_TIMEOUT_RUN_URL=$(find_latest_scoped_run_field "${TEST_REPO}" "${CLARIFY_CREATED_AFTER}" "Clarif" "${ISSUE_TITLE}" "html_url" 1 2>/dev/null) || CLARIFY_TIMEOUT_RUN_URL=""`. That is one page, one read, and no retry loop.
  - Print `echo "  Clarify run: ${CLARIFY_TIMEOUT_RUN_URL}"` only when the value matches `^https://[^[:space:]]+/actions/runs/[0-9]+$`.
  - If the value is empty or does not match, print nothing, or one plain "Clarify run: not found" line. Either way the step still ends with `status=timeout` and `exit 1`.
- Every `IDLE` comparison stays as `[ "$IDLE" -ge ...`; add no unquoted `$IDLE` operand.

### 2. Step "Wait for clarify→plan→implement (alt-model)" (`id: wait`, around line 5317)
- **env:** add `ALT_PRE_CLARIFY_RUN_ID: ${{ steps.create.outputs.pre_clarify_run_id }}` and `ALT_ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ steps.create.outputs.title }}`. Both names are unused in the file.
- **After the loop,** keep `echo "::error::Alt-model run timed out before reaching review stage"` exactly as it is; `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_alt_model_cleanup_pr_selector.py:184` pins it. Then add:
  - `echo "  Issue: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/${TEST_REPO}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}"`;
  - if `ALT_PRE_CLARIFY_RUN_ID` is a number, look up one run with `gh api "repos/${TEST_REPO}/actions/workflows/clarify.yml/runs?per_page=20" --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.id > ${ALT_PRE_CLARIFY_RUN_ID})] | sort_by(.created_at) | last | .html_url // empty" 2>/dev/null || echo ""`. This uses the same id-anchor pattern as the "Capture alt-model phase run ids" step;
  - print it through the same `https://…/actions/runs/<n>` regex guard, then `exit 1`.
- `ALT_ISSUE_TITLE` is optional. Use it only if it fits cheaply: filter `.display_title` with gojq's `env.ALT_ISSUE_TITLE`. Otherwise leave it out of the env.
- Do not change anything before the loop's `done`. The capacity block must stay before `body="/approved"`, which must stay before `grep -qE 'ai:done|`.

### 3. Contract tests (existing file only; append `test_` functions)
`main()` already finds every `test_*` function, so no wiring change is needed.

**Phase 1 harness** `_run_clarify_wait(tmp, comments_json, runs_json=None, runs_fail=False)`:
- Prepend shell-function fakes to the step body taken from `_step(_all_steps(_raw()), CLARIFY_STEP)["run"]`: `sleep() { :; }`, and a `gh()` that:
  - serves fixture JSON for the issue (labels `ai:clarifying`), for `*/comments*` and for `*actions/runs*` (exits 1 when `runs_fail` is set);
  - applies any `--jq EXPR` argument by piping through the real `jq -r`;
  - counts calls to the comments endpoint in a state file.
- Use shell functions, not PATH executables. The pre-push gate container mounts the temp dir noexec, as the comment in `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_alt_model_cleanup_pr_selector.py` around line 101 explains.
- Run with `cwd=REPO_ROOT`, because the step sources `./scripts/comprehensive_test_and_release_gh_api.sh`. Env: `PHASE_TIMEOUT` (`"0"` for the timeout case, `"30"` otherwise), `POLL_INTERVAL=0`, `TEST_REPO=o/r`, `ISSUE_NUMBER=42`, `ISSUE_TITLE`, `CLARIFY_CREATED_AFTER`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://github.com`, and a 60s timeout.
- Skip the test if bash or jq is missing.

**New tests:**
- `test_clarify_wait_fails_fast_on_clarify_failed_comment`:
  - An OWNER comment starting "AI clarification workflow failed for …" gives rc 1, `status=clarify_failed`, and the issue URL in stdout.
  - Comments per poll stay what they are on base. There is no extra endpoint: one `--jq length` read and one failure read per poll.
- `test_clarify_wait_ignores_untrusted_or_non_prefix_failure_comment`:
  - With `PHASE_TIMEOUT=0`, a `NONE`/`CONTRIBUTOR` author with the same text, an OWNER comment whose text sits mid-body, and the "was cancelled/timed out" variant all end in `status=timeout`, not `clarify_failed`.
- `test_clarify_wait_timeout_prints_issue_and_run_url`:
  - With `PHASE_TIMEOUT=0` and a runs fixture holding two matching Clarify runs, stdout has the issue URL and exactly one `/actions/runs/` URL, and `status=timeout`.
  - With `runs_fail=True`, a non-URL `html_url`, or a `::warning::` value, rc is still 1, `status=timeout`, and no run URL or injected text is printed.
- `test_clarify_and_alt_model_timeouts_print_issue_url` (static checks):
  - `_ordered(clarify, CAPACITY_STATUS, "status=clarify_failed", "Clarify phase stalled", "Clarify run: ")`.
  - `_ordered(alt, "Alt-model run timed out before reaching review stage", "/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}", "clarify.yml/runs", "/actions/runs/")`.
  - The `IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR")` filter is in the clarify body.
  - The clarify body has exactly one `comments?per_page=5&direction=desc` occurrence.
- The existing `test_capacity_edited_step_bodies_parse_as_bash` already runs `bash -n` on both edited steps.

### 4. `changelog.d/9223-release-gate-clarify-stall-diagnostics.md`
- `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`, then one bullet in the style of `changelog.d/9266-*`. It covers the `clarify_failed` fail-fast, the timeout output (issue URL plus at most one Clarify run URL) in Phase 1 and the alt-model gate, the fact that both are fail-open, and ends with `Refs #9223.`

## Data structures affected
- `wait-clarify` gets a new `status` value, `clarify_failed`. The Phase 8 summary (around line 3560) treats every non-`success` value as FAILED and prints it, so no consumer change is needed.
- New step-scoped variables: `CLARIFY_CREATED_AFTER`, `CLARIFY_ISSUE_URL`, `CLARIFY_POLL_COMMENTS_JSON`, `CLARIFY_FAILED_COMMENTS`, `CLARIFY_TIMEOUT_RUN_URL`, `ALT_PRE_CLARIFY_RUN_ID`, and optionally `ALT_ISSUE_TITLE`. None of these names appears in the file today.
